fichas.title: Restaurant dining dimensions and clearances
fichas.summary: Guidance for comfortable dining describes personal table area, suitable table widths and depths, and clearances between tables, chairs, walls, and diners. Round tables may require additional space.

dimensions.label: Table area width per person
dimensions.context: Approximate width of table area required per diner.
dimensions.ocr_raw:

To be able to eat in comfort, one person requires a table area
around 60 em wide and 30-40 em deep -7 f) - 0. This provides
sufficient distance between adjacent diners. Although an additional
20 em space in the centre for dishes and large bowls is sometimes
desirable, an overall width of 80-85 em is suitable for a dining
table. If the food is served on plates, then 70 em is sufficient, and
for fast food 60 em table depth.
Distance between table and wall ;;;;75 em -7 0, because the chair
alone requires a space of 50 em. If the space between table and
wall is also used for access, the distance should be ;;;;1 00 em.
Round tables need a little more space, a difference of up to 50 em.

75

fichas.title: Space required for waiter and diner
fichas.summary: Illustrations show spatial arrangements and dimensions for diners seated at tables and for waiter movement and service around them.

fichas.title: Breakfast and dinner place settings
fichas.summary: Diagrams identify tableware and glassware for breakfast, informal dinner, and formal dinner settings. The page also illustrates space around settings.

fichas.title: Tables and seating layouts
fichas.summary: A range of illustrated table configurations shows seating arrangements for different group sizes, including rectangular, round, and other shaped tables. Dimension labels accompany some layouts.
